## ff39ea40ffdc

**Reproduced generated-lesson ambiguity.** Generator SHA-256
`490c2be77e1ced1a2fa75db88d40c603a7f28e24cd3686bb558b604c001b39de`; selected rule
hash `15dc7a8d8bc0`.

At seed `0`, medium difficulty, consecutive valid emissions at sample indices
`21,22,23,24` have rank controls `[1,1,1,3]` and transform controls `[4,4,6,6]`. Treating the
first three as demonstrations and the fourth as query leaves rank 3 entirely unseen.

The plausible rival `rank_3_selects_smallest` behaves identically for ranks 1 and 2 but,
when control 3 appears, chooses the smallest object instead of the largest. It fits all 5/5
canonical pairs because the canonical set contains no rank-3 case. It also fits all 3/3
demonstrations in this emitted window, but on the query the selected authority returns the
largest color-9 2×3 crop while the rival returns the smallest color-8 2×1 crop.

All four inputs pass the target `self_check`. Their selected outputs were obtained together
through the supported command:

```text
# cwd: packet_root
python3 run_with_racket.py python3 -m arcpuzzles apply ff39ea40ffdc \
  --input ../checks/audit/ff39ea40ffdc/input.json \
  --out ../checks/audit/ff39ea40ffdc/racket.json
```

Evidence: `checks/audit/ff39ea40ffdc/generation.json`,
`checks/audit/ff39ea40ffdc/racket.json`, and
`checks/audit/ff39ea40ffdc/rival.json`.

**Domain limitation.** This is an exact fixed-seed window of four consecutive generator
emissions, not a measured frequency over the production lesson assembler. The generator has
no teaching schedule that prevents such a window, so it is a concrete possible lesson under
consecutive assembly, but I did not estimate its probability under every downstream sampler.

**Recommendation.** Add a lesson contract or deterministic rank schedule that ensures the
three demonstrations cover every rank control relevant to the query, declare rank-based
competitors, and run production plus query-rotation census checks.
